translationRepairs: His uncle Zong Que, Jingzhou inspector, once set out vessels to test his nephews.
His uncle Zong Que, Yongzhou inspector, once set out vessels to test his nephews.
s0049 has 雍州刺史, so the inspectorate is Yongzhou; Jingzhou (荊州) is unsupported.
His uncle, Jingzhou inspector Zong Que, once set out vessels and tested his nephews.
His uncle, Yongzhou inspector Zong Que, once set out vessels and tested his nephews.
The same unit names 雍州刺史; replacing Jingzhou with Yongzhou restores the Chinese place title.
Song's Prince of Pingyang, inspector of Jingzhou, made him chief clerk.
Song's Prince of Jianping, inspector of Jingzhou, made him chief clerk.
宋建平王景素 is the Prince of Jianping; Pingyang (平陽) is not in the Chinese.
Song's Prince of Pingyang Jingsu was inspector of Jingzhou and summoned him as chief clerk.
Song's Prince of Jianping Jingsu was inspector of Jingzhou and summoned him as chief clerk.
Literal likewise misreads 建平 as Pingyang; Jianping matches 建平王景素.
Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao, Wuling grand administrator, prized his rule; when Diao became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai a staff officer and head clerk, sharing provincial affairs.
Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Yi, Wuling grand administrator, prized his rule; when Yi became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai a staff officer and head clerk, sharing provincial affairs.
齊豫章王嶷 uses the personal name 嶷, read Yi; Diao is a false romanization.

At the time Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao was grand administrator of Wuling and greatly prized Ai's governance; when Diao became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai staff officer on the chief of staff's staff and head clerk of the province, sharing in provincial affairs.

At the time Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Yi was grand administrator of Wuling and greatly prized Ai's governance; when Yi became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai staff officer on the chief of staff's staff and head clerk of the province, sharing in provincial affairs.
Both 嶷 mentions in s0056 are the same person; English Diao must be Yi.
Diao asked about custom, walls, temples, and passes; Ai answered as from a map, and Diao esteemed him more.
Yi asked about custom, walls, temples, and passes; Ai answered as from a map, and Yi esteemed him more.
Subject 嶷 continues the Prince of Yuzhang; replace Diao with Yi.

Diao once asked him about local custom, old ways, city walls and foundations, temples, and mountain passes—Ai answered each question on the spot as if reading from a gazetteer, and Diao esteemed him the more.

Yi once asked him about local custom, old ways, city walls and foundations, temples, and mountain passes—Ai answered each question on the spot as if reading from a gazetteer, and Yi esteemed him the more.
Literal agents are 嶷; Yi is the correct reading, not Diao.
Envious men said his gate was a market; Diao watched and found him reading behind closed doors.
Envious men said his gate was a market; Yi watched and found him reading behind closed doors.
嶷遣覘之 names the same 嶷; correcting Diao to Yi fixes the personal name without other change.
Provincial men envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was like a market; Diao sent men to watch and found Ai behind closed doors reading.
Provincial men envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was like a market; Yi sent men to watch and found Ai behind closed doors reading.
Literal subject of 遣覘之 is 嶷 (Yi), not Diao.
Diao returned to court; Ai became Grand Marshal punitive staff officer, ran the secretariat, then Zhijiang magistrate.
Yi returned to court; Ai became Grand Marshal punitive staff officer, ran the secretariat, then Zhijiang magistrate.
嶷還都 continues the same prince; Yi replaces the erroneous Diao.
When Diao returned to the capital, Ai was made staff officer on the Grand Marshal's punitive staff, in charge of the secretariat, then magistrate of Zhijiang.
When Yi returned to the capital, Ai was made staff officer on the Grand Marshal's punitive staff, in charge of the secretariat, then magistrate of Zhijiang.
Literal likewise depends on 嶷; the personal name is Yi.
In year nine Prince Diao died; Ai mourned, led old Jing and Xiang clerks, and raised a tomb stele.
In year nine Prince Yi died; Ai mourned, led old Jing and Xiang clerks, and raised a tomb stele.
豫章王嶷薨 again names 嶷; Prince Yi is required, not Prince Diao.
In year nine the Prince of Yuzhang Diao died; Ai left office to mourn, led former clerks of Jing and Xiang, and set a stele at the tomb.
In year nine the Prince of Yuzhang Yi died; Ai left office to mourn, led former clerks of Jing and Xiang, and set a stele at the tomb.
Literal death notice has 豫章王嶷; replace Diao with Yi.
Prince Xuan of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
長沙宣武王 is the compound posthumous title Xuanwu of Changsha; Prince Xuan splits and truncates 宣武.
At the time the Prince of Changsha, King Xuan of Wu, was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.
At the time King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.
宣武王 is one posthumous name Xuanwu, not King Xuan of Wu; the proposed King Xuanwu of Changsha matches the Chinese.
